Iḷā
------------------------------------------
The Ṛgveda (1.13.9) mentions Iḷā along with सरस्वती and Mahī—as a goddess of light and brilliance. She is the goddess of the earth. In another place (1.31.11) she is declared as the daughter of मनु and the teacher of men. Her place is the centre of the earth. On the sacrificial altar, the place sanctified by her feet, is used for keeping the fire of the sacrifice.
In the पुराणस् and the Mahābhārata, she is pictured as the daughter of मनु. Due to several reasons like entering a forbidden place or the efforts of the sages like वसिष्ठ she undergoes change of sex, becoming the prince Sudyumna or the wife of बुध (and मोथेर् of पुरूरवस्) and so on. She used to undergo change of sex once a month!
See also IḌĀ.
